title: On the localization transition from MAA to AA models
abstract: Despite their potential similarity between the mosaic Aubry-André (MAA) and AA models, the MAA model allows mobility edges (MEs), whereas the AA model does not. Here we develop a new double quasiperiodic MAA (DMAA) model consisting of one primitive MAA with nonzero even-site potentials and the other modified one with both nonzero odd-site potentials and a tunable amplitude factor, to reveal how localization transitions evolve from MAA to AA models. Interplays and competitions among the extended, critical and localized states arising from superpositions of double quasi-periodic MAA potentials enable new twice and multiple localization-delocalization transitions besides the original single localization transition. Our numerical calculations on inverse participation ratio, normalized participation ratio, fractal dimension and real-space wavefunction distribution confirm such localization features. The continuum model simulations on the experimental polariton modes also yield consistent results and hence validate their experimental feasibility. The constructed DMAA model provides a new framework for studying the localization transition processes between two analogous quasiperiodic models and broadens the understanding of Anderson localization.
summary: This paper introduces the Double Quasiperiodic MAA (DMAA) model to study the transition from MAA to AA type quasiperiodic potentials. By analyzing diagnostic quantities like IPR and fractal dimension, the authors demonstrate that this evolution reveals multiple localization-delocalization transitions not present in simpler models. The findings are validated using both numerical simulations and continuum models relevant for experimental platforms.
main_problem: The study aims to reveal how localization transitions evolve when moving from Mosaic Aubry-André (MAA) models to standard Aubry-André (AA) models.
main_result: The Double Quasiperiodic MAA (DMAA) model exhibits new twice and multiple localization-delocalization transitions, which are absent in the original AA model.
method: Numerical calculations were performed using diagnostic quantities like Inverse Participation Ratio (IPR), Normalized Participation Ratio (NPR), and Fractal Dimension ($Q$) on both tight-binding and continuum models.
model_or_system: The Double Quasiperiodic MAA (DMAA) model is a one-dimensional chain governed by a Hamiltonian with double quasiperiodic on-site potentials. The transition between MAA ($ eta=0$) and AA ($ eta=1$) is controlled by the tunable amplitude factor $ eta$.
key_observables: Inverse Participation Ratio (IPR), Normalized Participation Ratio (NPR), Fractal Dimension ($Q$), and real-space wavefunction distribution.
important_parameters: Potential strength ($\lambda$), tuning parameter ($ eta \in [0, 1]$), and energy ($E_n$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the DMAA model providing a continuous framework to study the transition between MAA and AA models.
figures_summary: Figures show $Q$ vs. energy for varying $ eta$, confirming Mobility Edges in MAA but not AA; other figures plot IPR/NPR changes demonstrating multiple transitions at specific parameter regimes.
paper_structure: The paper develops the DMAA model, analyzes its behavior across different disorder strengths ($\lambda$) and tuning parameters ($ eta$), uses various diagnostic tools (IPR, NPR, Q), and validates findings by comparing tight-binding results with continuum simulations applicable to polariton modes.
why_interesting: It provides a detailed theoretical framework for understanding how the nature of localization transitions changes when moving between two closely related quasiperiodic models, which has implications for disordered quantum systems in photonics or cold atoms.
